claims.statement: The how-to parent links account management, account settings, profile customization, contribution settings, organization membership and email preferences across products. Parent wildcard versions do not override child product, version or actor restrictions.

The account/profile landing page spans FPT/GHES/GHEC, routes to get-started, concepts, how-tos, tutorials and reference, and curates nine recommendations and seven categories. Carousels and category inclusion are navigation, not semantic review, feature entitlement or adopted policy.

The reference parent lists profile, personal dashboard, profile contributions, email addresses, personal account and username references across products. Listing an artifact is not its completed review or published-version assurance.

Cloud public-profile details carry identity-disclosure risks and sharing is the user's choice. Displayed names may also appear beside comments in organization-owned private repositories; social-account links are visible to viewers of the profile. These are field-specific exposure claims, not authorization to disclose personal information.

Pronouns are available FPT/GHEC through the feature dataset, and the reusable says only signed-in users can see them. This audience differs from generic public-profile visibility; GHES availability and unauthenticated visibility must not be inferred.

A default identicon derives from user-ID hash with no chosen color/pattern; replacement images use PNG/JPG/GIF, strictly less than 1 MB and smaller than 3000 by 3000 pixels. About 500 by 500 is a quality recommendation, not another mandatory limit.

An email-associated Gravatar can be the default image and uploaded GitHub images override it. The GHEC branch excludes Gravatar for enterprise managed users. Email association and image display do not prove mailbox custody or account authentication.

Status can appear on profile, hovercards, team pages and organization dashboards. Busy both displays availability notices on mentions/assignment/review requests and excludes the person from automatic review assignment for their teams; this preference can affect review workflow and is not evidence that manual requests are blocked.

Location and timezone disclose local time on profile and hovercards. Self-view shows relation to UTC, while other viewers see difference from their own local time; optional disclosure and display semantics are not legal jurisdiction, authenticated location or availability proof.

Public repositories may be pinned when owned or contributed to within the last year; fork commits do not qualify for pinning a nonowned fork. Public owned gists may be pinned. Star counts and gist opening lines appear, and pinned items replace the popular section; pins are curated, not exhaustive ownership or activity inventory.

The FPT private-profile limitations prohibit Sponsors eligibility, do not remove/hide past activity, apply while private mode is enabled, leave public-repository activity visible at the repository and may leave some API activity available. Private profile is not historical erasure, repository privacy or complete API nondisclosure.

FPT/GHEC program badges describe Developer Program membership, Pro subscription, bounty contribution, Campus Expert participation and accepted advisory credit. These separate conditions do not justify buying plans, enrolling in programs or using badges as universal engineering competence or effective-security proof.

FPT/GHEC Achievements are event-based badges with event links restricted to viewers having repository/organization access; the feature is public preview and subject to change. Hidden links do not prove every badge reveals no private metadata, and achievement visibility remains an owner-controlled preference.

FPT/GHEC managed-enterprise profile-name changes must occur through the identity provider, not GitHub. This display-name rule is separate from username-change authority and cannot grant agent control over the IdP.
Mentioning a member organization in the bio prioritizes it in the activity overview. This presentation order is not a role, authorization, employment or organization-ownership assertion.

The Mars 2020 Helicopter Contributor event has ended and its badge is no longer available. The full historical repository/version/tag table, based on JPL information, is reference evidence rather than current dependency recommendations, installation authority, source ingestion of linked repositories or a present qualification pathway.
